question.text: In the 20th century, this Southern Hemisphere country built a nearly 3500-mile fence to keep dingos, a type of wild dog that lives in this country's outback, out of its more populated southeast.
question.clue: This nation's Prime Minister, Harold Holt, headed the UAP and was presumed to have drowned while swimming in a resort town.

swap.leadin: Descendents of convicts known as "currency lads" carried out raids on feral horses called brumbies in the bush and this region.
swap.text: Name this region where jackaroos established "cattle empires" around stations. The disastrous Emu War occurred in this rural region of central Australia.
swap.clue: An overland telegraph line through this region was scouted by Robert Burke and William Wills but was eventually built through Alice Springs.

question.text: The "history wars" began after the Bringing Them Home report was released on these people. This term refers to Australian Aborigines taken from their families as children by the Australian government.
question.clue: An official 2007 apology to these people and their descendants was made by then-Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

swap.leadin: This colony was founded by the First Fleet on January 26, 1788, and its first governor was Arthur Phillip.
swap.text: Name this colony which originated around Port Jackson. Lachlan Macquarie was the final governor of this territory.
swap.clue: George Johnston and John Macarthur led forces during an 1808 event in this colony.

question.leadin: Australia has struggled with the civil rights of these people.
question.text: These indigenous Australians were frequently massacred at the beginning of British colonization of Australia.
question.clue: Many of these people were taken from their families and integrated into white culture, becoming the Stolen Generation.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the only successful armed uprising in Australian history.
swap.text: Major George Johnston invaded Government House and placed Bligh under arrest in this capital city of New South Wales.
swap.clue: Lachlan Macquarie ("LACK-lan muh-KWAIR-ee") was placed in charge of this city after John Macarthur overthrew governor William Bligh in the Rum Rebellion.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a World War I battle.
question.text: This military group, composed of soldiers from two nations, landed at Gallipoli at its namesake cove, but was disbanded after the campaign's failure.
question.answer: Australian and New Zealand Army Corps
question.clue: Alexander Godley collaborated with William Birdwood to oversee its operations, which didn't formally cease until another branch of it disbanded after Villers-Bretonneux.

swap.leadin: As Treasurer of Australia, this man oversaw the creation of the Australian Dollar and later ended the pegging of the currency to the British pound.
swap.text: Name this Prime Minister who more famously went missing while swimming at Cheviot Beach in 1967. Ironically, a swimming pool in Melbourne was named in his honor.
swap.clue: This prime minister declared that he was "all the way with LBJ" in showing his country's support for the Vietnam War.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the "White Australia" policy of discrimination.
question.text: This Australian prime minister began dismantling White Australia in 1966, a year before his mysterious disappearance during a swimming incident while in office.
question.clue: One ruler of this name allied with Tostig to fight against another ruler with this name at Stamford Bridge.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about modern gun control measures around the world.
swap.text: Australian Prime Minister John Howard implemented a gun buyback program and severely restricted private gun ownership following this 1996 mass shooting in Tasmania.
swap.clue: This November 1894 event carried out by General Yamaji Motoharu's forces, which killed somewhere between 1,000 and 20,000 people.

question.text: One of the most famous people from Victoria was this leader of the Greta Mob. This man killed three policemen at Stringybark Creek and also dictated the Jerilderie Letter.
question.clue: This man sent a lewd note wrapped around calves' testicles to Jeremiah McCormack's wife.

swap.text: In this 1854 incident, miners at the namesake stockade in Victoria waged a failed rebellion against the colonial government. The miners argued for the right to vote and the reduction of license fees.
swap.answerHtml: Eureka Rebellion [accept synonyms for rebellion, accept Eureka Stockade]
swap.clue: The battle of this event saw one leader stop 100 fighters from being bayoneted by troops under a commander who later went on to serve in the second opium war, J.W. Thomas.

question.leadin: A 1920 act titled "Protection of" [this word] bans using this word for commercial purposes, except when referring to its namesake oatmeal coconut "biscuits."
question.text: What word names an April 25th holiday that commemorates the amphibious landing of an Army Corps made up of forces from two Commonwealth countries, as well as the cove where they landed?
question.clue: Their most notable action is remembered in the song titled "And the Band Played" a certain nationalist folk tune, was supported by the French from Kum Kale, and was advocated by Winston Churchill.

swap.text: Eddie Mabo taught the Papuan Meriam language to children from these islands off the coast of Queensland's Cape York Peninsula. Together with the Aborigines, the Melanesian people of these islands form Australia's Indigenous community.
swap.answerHtml: Torres Strait Islands [accept Torres Strait Islanders; reject “Torres Islands”]
swap.clue: This strait, named for a Spanish explorer, is home to namesake islands populated by indigenous Melanesian people and located between the Cape York Peninsula and the island of New Guinea.

question.text: A landmark 1891 sheep shearers' strike led to the founding of this party under the "Tree of Knowledge." This party's later leaders included Billy Hughes and Gough Whitlam.
question.answerHtml: Australian Labor Party [or ALP; prompt on Labor Party with “of what country?”]
question.clue: This political party passed important social reforms under leaders like Bob Hawke and Gough Whitlam.

swap.text: Menzies built credit among the middle class by calling them by this name, which titles a notable 1942 speech he made emphasizing his connections to ordinary people.

question.leadin: A famous cartoon of this event depicts the Governor of the territory in which it took place cowering under his bed.
question.text: Name this uprising, led by George Macarthur. Macarthur was angered by, among other things, a lien against one of his ships for abetting an escaped convict and Major George Johnston.
question.clue: This rebellion took place after the arrest of John Macarthur, a lieutenant of the New South Wales Corp. It was named for the nickname of the New South Wales Corp, which had to do with a product the Corp traded.

swap.leadin: An incredibly strong worker known as Crooked Mick appears in folktales about a mythical one of these places called the Speewah.
swap.text: Name these places, such as Anna Creek and Victoria Downs. Subsidiaries of these places, prefixed with the word "out-," also name remote communities of Aboriginal Australians.
swap.answerHtml: stations [accept cattle stations; accept sheep stations; accept outstations; prompt on cattle ranches]

question.text: Later, New Zealand and Australia laid out their post-WWII military and political goals in the Canberra Pact, signed by this Australian prime minister. Frank Forde finished this prime minister's term after his death in office.
question.clue: This prime minister of Australia during World War Two, a member of the Labour Party, defended the policy by declaring the country "the home of the British race" in a 1942 speech.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of convict-era Australia.
swap.text: The Australian-born children of emancipated convicts were known by this term, contrasted with "sterling" or English-born settlers.
swap.clue: Edible examples of these items include Mongolian tea bricks, and, in Rome, salt.
